name: Woodall v. Federal Bureau of Prisons
summary: The Third Circuit ruled that a federal prisoner could use a § 2241 habeas petition to challenge a Bureau of Prisons regulation that limited his transfer to a community corrections center, because the claim related to the execution of his sentence.
significance: This Third Circuit case held that a prisoner's challenge to the Bureau of Prisons' policy limiting placement in a community corrections center could be brought through § 2241 habeas, supporting the argument that claims about placement in less restrictive custody are cognizable in habeas.
